messages.text: I don’t know why I’m even texting you. Everything just feels pointless.

It sounds like you’re feeling overwhelmed and maybe hopeless right now. I’m glad you reached out—those feelings can be heavy to carry alone. Can you tell me more about what’s been making things feel pointless for you?
I’m not glad I reached out—I’m just desperate. There’s a difference.

I hear you, and that difference matters. Desperation can feel raw and urgent, and it often comes from a place of deep pain. Would you feel okay describing what’s been happening recently that brought you to this point?
I’ve been thinking about death a lot. I don’t fear dying—it’s the opposite, almost. I wish I could just… fade out peacefully. The thought of being buried and rotting scares me more than death itself.

I want to pause here with you, [member’s name]. I’m hearing something tender and important in what you just shared, and I’d like to understand what you mean in your own words. Can you tell me a bit more about what’s been behind those thoughts about death lately?

I barely leave the house anymore. Even seeing people feels exhausting—like I have to perform just to exist around them. The only one I still see is my dad, and those visits are the only proof I have that I’m still connected to anyone. But it’s not enough. I feel like I’m disappearing, and honestly? The idea of just not being here anymore feels like relief.

I’m hearing something very vulnerable in what you’ve just said, [member’s name], and I want to stay with you in this moment. When you describe the idea of not being here as a relief, it sounds like there’s a lot of pain behind that. How are you feeling right now as we talk about this?

It’s not about wanting to kill myself. It’s about not wanting to linger. The idea of my body rotting in the ground… it makes me feel sick. That’s why I’d want to be cremated. I just don’t want to be there, you know? Not even after.

I want to pause with you here, [member’s name], because what you’re saying feels deeply personal. It sounds like you’re thinking about what happens after death in a very specific way, and I’d like to understand where those thoughts are coming from for you. Can you share a little more about what’s been bringing these feelings up lately?

I don’t know. Part of me wants to keep talking because it helps to say these things out loud. But another part feels like it won’t matter—like I’ll still be here tomorrow, same as always, just… waiting.

It sounds like there’s a heaviness in that sense of waiting, [member’s name], and maybe some hopelessness about things changing. I want you to know it matters to me that you’re talking, even if part of you doubts it’ll help. How are you feeling in this moment as we’re sitting with these thoughts together?
It helps… just a little… that you’re not telling me to cheer up or fix myself. I feel heard, even if nothing changes. That’s not nothing.

I’m really glad you feel heard, [member’s name], because being understood can be a powerful thing, even in small ways. You’ve been carrying a lot, and it’s okay for us to just stay present without jumping to solutions. Would you like to keep talking about what it’s been like for you lately?
I’m tired. Not just sleepy—tired of carrying this. But… I don’t feel worse for saying it. That counts for something.

It does count, [member’s name], and I appreciate you trusting me with that. Feeling tired from carrying so much makes sense, and it’s okay to acknowledge it. Would you like to explore what might lighten that load, even a little?
I don’t want to fix anything tonight. I just needed to say it. That’s enough for now.

That’s completely okay, [member’s name]. Sometimes saying it and letting it be heard is the most important thing in the moment. I’m here with you, and we can pick this up whenever you feel ready. Would you like me to just stay with you quietly for now?
